name: Curtis Mayfield
hook: Started his own label to own his own masters, then years after an accident left him paralyzed, finished an album by singing a line at a time from his back.
blurb: Curtis Mayfield began recording with the Impressions in 1958, and by the late 1960s was writing directly about Black pride and civil rights on songs like 'People Get Ready' and 'Choice of Colors'. In 1968 he and manager Eddie Thomas started Curtom Records so Mayfield could own his own recordings rather than sign them away, part of a pattern on this map of Black artists taking control of their own recordings, alongside Ariwa and Rockers International, and like Kling Klang. His records, especially the 1972 'Super Fly' soundtrack, are among the most heavily sampled sources in hip-hop. In 1990 a lighting rig fell on him during an outdoor concert and left him paralysed from the neck down. He kept recording anyway, lying on his back and singing a line at a time so engineers could piece the vocal together. He needed help with his breathing to hold a vocal line, and what once took minutes took hours. He finished the album 'New World Order' in 1996.

signatureTracks.title: People Get Ready (The Impressions)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A civil-rights-era gospel-soul anthem, still one of the most covered songs of the period.
